text:
katie_oncall: Heads-up — we're seeing GPU capacity degradation in us-west-2 (region-3). Autoscaler kicked, but some traffic is still landing on the old region. Symptoms look like DNS cache/TTL propagation rather than pure routing. Can neteng confirm? :warning:
marcus_neteng: Confirmed. Lots of clients/partners still resolving to the us-west-2 endpoint. I ran `dig` from 3 external resolvers, TTLs vary wildly and some edges still have >300s left. Example: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 inference.example.com` returned old A set.
lee_sre: We already started shifting traffic to us-east-1 via routing policy (weighted failover -> 0.0.0.0 for us-west). But DNS caches and some CDNs are sticking to old IPs. Lowering TTL now is still useful for future queries but won't expire existing cached entries.
katie_oncall: What's the fastest mitigation to reduce user-facing 5xx/latency from the degraded region?
tina_runtime: Two prongs: (1) accelerate cache eviction at major CDNs/partners (purge API) and (2) inject dynamic fallback via our edge LB: advertise a 503-based redirect or proxy to us-east for connections to the old IPs. But proxying increases egress and GPU load in us-east, so we must throttle non-critical jobs.
marcus_neteng: I'll open purge requests to the three largest CDN providers now. Request payloads and curl examples: ```bash
# Akamai purge
curl -X POST "https://api.akamai.com/ccu/v3/invalidate/url" -H "Authorization: Bearer $AK_API" -d '{"objects":["https://inference.example.com/"]}'
# Cloudfront invalidation
aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id $DISTID --paths "/"
```
lee_sre: Also, change DNS record set to add an ALIAS of inference.example.com -> failover.example.net which points to us-east IP set. That gives us ability to rotate underlying A records without changing customer-visible name. I'm going to patch the zone via our DNS API. Note: TTL will be set to 30s to speed subsequent resolution.
katie_oncall: Reminder: changing TTL doesn't flush existing caches. We should notify the biggest partners (cdn partners, enterprise customers) to flush their caches. I'll draft an incident email list.
marcus_neteng: Applied zone change (via DNS API). New record: `inference.example.com CNAME failover.example.net` + TTL=30. DNS provider shows change propagated to authoritative nameservers. Waiting on external resolver tests.
dns-bot: zone-update accepted: zone=example.com change_id=chg_987654321 status=applied timestamp=1823456830
lee_sre: Quick tests: `dig +trace inference.example.com` on our jump shows CNAME in place. External checks: 2/5 public resolvers now return the new failover IPs. Some large resolver clusters (ISP caches) still have old A records until their TTL expires.
tina_runtime: To reduce load on us-east while propagation finishes: set admission-control to 'critical-only' for GPU pods, drain batch jobs/low-priority queues, and raise model-quantization to reduce memory per-request. Commands: ```bash
# cordon non-critical nodes
kubectl label node gpu-node-12 shard=drain
# scale down batch worker pool
kubectl scale deploy batch-workers --replicas=2
```
marcus_neteng: FYI we can add a negative DNS TTL hack: issue an immediate SOA serial bump with a very small TTL on a separate A record used by partners that obey it. Not guaranteed but worth trying with partners who support low TTLs. I'm pinging partner-ops.
katie_oncall: Good. I'm coordinating partner ops pings. Also notify Billing/CS about potential short-term egress/capacity cost uptick if we proxy.
lee_sre: Monitoring: watch `5xx_rate`, `latency_p95`, synthetic checks, DNS error logs. I'm creating a dashboard panel and will post updates.
dns-bot: partner-purge-status: akamai=queued cloudfront=invalidating fastly=completed
marcus_neteng: Partner ops confirmed they'll flush for 3 major enterprise customers (on request). They reported one older firewall appliance that does long-lived DNS caching (won't respect TTL) — we may need to provide IP allowlist change guidance to that customer.
tina_runtime: If propagation drags, we should be ready to fallback to our L4 anycast announcement for the old prefixes and sink traffic there with a blackhole/proxy. That requires NOC coordination for BGP. @marcus_neteng can you prep the BGP runbook?
marcus_neteng: On it. BGP prep: locate prefix, prepend community, coordinate with transit provider. Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/dns-failover (ping me before route-change).
katie_oncall: Timeline: zone change at +20s, CDN purges +30s, partner flush confirmations +60-120s, continue monitoring. If error rates across production don't drop in 10m, escalate to route-level failover.
lee_sre: Noted. Updating incident channel and will add postmortem bullet about long TTLs and partner caching behavior. We should add a permanent step: set emergency pre-failover TTL to 60s for future use and document which partner contacts to ping automatically.
katie_oncall: Thanks team. Keep short updates here. :thumbsup:
